title: AMU students protest demanding restoration of student union elections
seoTitle: Aligarh: AMU students demand union elections

tea.why: Students protest the lack of student union elections for seven years and the suspension of a student leader who demanded elections.
tea.want: Restoration of the AMU Student Union, conduct of elections, and release of an election notification within 48 hours.
tea.changed: Oct 5: Student Yasir Fahad continues an indefinite hunger strike, which has been ongoing for 14 days.

summary: Students at Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) have been protesting for 14 days, demanding the restoration of the AMU Student Union and the conduct of elections, which have not occurred for nearly seven years. The agitation began after female students protested poor food quality, alleging insects in their meals. Following this, student Yasir Fahad submitted a memorandum demanding union elections and a notification within 48 hours. The AMU administration responded by suspending Fahad, citing his involvement in an "illegal protest" and road blocking. In response to his suspension, Fahad began an indefinite hunger strike, which continues without constructive dialogue from the university administration. The Students' Federation of India (SFI), AMU unit, has expressed support for the students.
organizers: Students' Federation of India (SFI), AMU unit
response: The AMU administration suspended student Yasir Fahad, alleging his involvement in an "illegal protest" and blocking a road. No constructive dialogue has been reported between the administration and the protesting students.
